column8: PGmc `*θánxtē` 'thought (3sg pret.)' > OE `þōhte`. SC103 creates the nasalized low vowel and deletes the nasal (`*θ*á*n*x*t*ē` > `*θ*ã*x*t*ē`); SC104 then rounds exactly that vowel (`*θ*ã*x*t*ē` > `*θ*ō*x*t*ē`). Counterfactual composition in the opposite order leaves `*θ*ã*x*t*ē` unrounded, because SC104 has no `{*ã}` to read until SC103 has applied — a live feeding relation, not merely a stage entailment. This is the low-vowel (*aNx) branch of SC103; the high-vowel branch, exemplified by `fist` (`*fúnxstiz`), never reaches SC104
column12: Live feeding relation with a low-vowel corpus witness: `thought` (PGmc *θánxtē > OE þōhte), added 2026 precisely because SC103's low-vowel branch previously had no live witness. A Proto-Germanic change necessarily precedes an Anglo-Frisian one, and the corpus now also demonstrates the feeding directly. Campbell §128 n.1 p.50 states that the rounding affected the nasalized vowel of §119 (this rule) and of §121 (SC026/SC027) at the same time; Fulk §4.11 p.72 adds that Old Saxon reflects the PGmc nasalized vowel invariably as unrounded ā, which is the comparative proof that the rounding is later and narrower than SC103; Fulk §4.1 p. 55 names OE pret. sg. þōhte as the very form in which the PGmc nasalized vowel surfaces as Anglo-Frisian ō.

column12: Stage-entailed, NOT independently demonstrated. The direction therefore follows from the established stages alone. In the executable cascade SC103 does create the *xst cluster that SC028 simplifies in fist (*funxstiz > *fuxstiz > *fustiz), but that feeding is NOT a chronology demonstration: a counterfactual composition with SC028 before SC103 still yields fyst, because deleting the *x first leaves *funstiz, whose nasal is then removed with compensatory lengthening by the Ingvaeonic nasal-spirant law SC026/SC027 (whose domain includes *ns). The surface result is overdetermined, so no corpus witness discriminates the order and none is claimed. See sc028-xs-cluster-simplification-adjudication.md. Witness discipline: fist is named as the representative lexeme because it is the form in which the relation is visible, but it is NOT a discriminating witness. A counterfactual run with SC028 composed before SC103 still yields fyst, because deleting the *x first leaves a nasal before *s which the Ingvaeonic nasal-spirant law then removes with the same compensatory lengthening. The outcome is overdetermined, so no corpus form can demonstrate the order and no machine evidence route is claimed.

column12: Feeding, established by the scholarship and machine-verified. SC010 geminates *w before *j (Campbell §407 p.167: 'every consonant except r being affected after short syllables... The forms in which w is doubled are dealt with in §120.2'; R/T p.53: 'it appears that that cluster too underwent gemination in PWGmc'), and SC029 then resolves the geminate it creates. Both handbooks present the two as successive stages of one history: R/T p.53 write PNWGmc *awj > PWGmc *[aw'w'] > pre-OE *[auj], and Campbell §120.2 p.46 writes the ordered chain 'auj > auuj > auj'. The direction is therefore historical, not merely executable. The West Germanic intermediate is independently attested in the continental cognates (OHG houwi, gistrouwen; OS hoi). Before the 2026 repair CAPR had no rule creating this geminate and fed hay with it lexically; see sc010-w-gemination-and-hay-depth-adjudication.md.
